caption:
Most small businesses don't fail because they stop making money. They fail because they lose track of it.

If your business and personal money still share one account, you're not behind — you're just at the starting line most owners never cross.

Three small moves that change everything:
1. Open a separate business checking account.
2. Reconcile it monthly — match every transaction to a record.
3. Keep your receipts in one place.

Clarity isn't about being perfect with money. It's about being honest with it — so you can steward what you've been given with confidence.

Before you build, count the cost. We're here to help you count it well.

Follow @countthecostbk for a simple bookkeeping tip every week.

#SmallBusiness #Bookkeeping #ChristianEntrepreneur #SmallBusinessTips #FaithAndBusiness #Stewardship #CountTheCost

"Whoever can be trusted with very little can also be trusted with much." — Luke 16:10

Faithful bookkeeping isn't about the size of your business. It's about how you handle what's in front of you today.

Every reconciled account, every tracked receipt, every honest number is a small act of stewardship. And small, faithful steps compound — into trust, into peace, into a business built on solid ground.

You don't need more before you can steward well. You can start with what you have.
